title: Cybersecurity & Zero-Trust
meta_description: Cybersecurity & Zero-Trust services from Dataq Software: scope, delivery pattern, platforms and committed outcomes.

blocks.x: Cybersecurity & Zero-Trust covers architecture-level security programs: zero-trust network and workload design, identity modernization, threat intelligence and managed detection, cloud posture management, AI-specific security for models and agents, cyber resilience, and the compliance machinery (SOC 2, ISO 27001, PCI DSS, DORA) that regulated industries must evidence. We design for the assumption of breach and the reality of audit.

The attack surface grew faster than the org chart: SaaS sprawl, machine identities outnumbering human ones, and AI systems that can be poisoned or prompted into leakage. Frameworks hardened in response — NIST CSF 2.0, DORA in the EU, SEC disclosure rules in the US — making security a board-level, evidence-first discipline.
The services behind Cyber & Zero-Trust, each page carrying the full build pattern:

items: Zero-Trust Architecture & Implementation
Never trust, always verify — zero-trust as an executable architecture, not a slide.
Threat Intelligence & Managed SOC
Detection that keeps pace — intelligence-driven SOC with the boring parts (tuning, coverage) done properly.
Identity & Access Modernization
Identity as the perimeter — workforce, customer and machine identities on one governed plane.
Cloud Security & Posture Management
Secure at the control plane — posture, workload and data security engineered into the platform.
AI Security & Model Protection
Secure the models themselves — prompt-injection defense, agent containment and AI red-teaming.
Cyber Resilience & Incident Recovery
Assume breach, plan recovery — resilience engineered, rehearsed and measured.
Compliance, Audit & Digital Trust
Evidence once, audit anywhere — compliance automation across SOC 2, ISO 27001, PCI DSS, DORA and privacy.

blocks.x: What a Cyber & Zero-Trust engagement shares across services: the baseline is signed, the slice is bounded, and the gates can stop the program — that last part is a feature. Baselines are signed in the first two weeks, the working slice lands inside the quarter, and the value ledger stays open to your finance team.

The next step is small and real: one working session on Cybersecurity & Zero-Trust, your data, and a written feasibility read you can circulate.
